findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it a public IP and exposing the MySQL endpoint to the internet, where only the security group stands between attackers and the database.
storage_encrypted = false means the database volume and snapshots are stored unencrypted, exposing catalog data if the underlying storage or a snapshot is accessed.

The master password is supplied through var.password and passed in plaintext to the resource; it is stored in Terraform state unencrypted and also interpolated into EC2 user data, leaking the credential. Using AWS Secrets Manager / manage_master_user_password is preferred.
iam_database_authentication_enabled is not set, so only static password authentication is possible for the MySQL instance, preventing centralized, short-lived credential control.
skip_final_snapshot = true combined with backup_retention_period = 0 disables all recoverable copies, so data destruction (accidental or malicious) is irreversible.

The database master username and password are embedded in the instance user_data script, which is readable by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute or from the instance metadata service (including via SSRF from the web app), leaking database credentials.

metadata_options is not configured, so IMDSv1 remains available; combined with the plaintext credentials in user data and the overly permissive instance profile, an SSRF in the PHP app can retrieve role credentials and the DB password.
No root_block_device/ebs encryption configuration is specified, so the instance volume (which stores the dbinfo.inc file containing DB credentials) may be unencrypted at rest.

The instance role grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", allowing full control of all S3 buckets, EC2, and RDS in the account. Any compromise of the web server yields near-account-wide privileges.
The database security group allows all outbound traffic to 0.0.0.0/0 on all protocols and ports, enabling data exfiltration or command-and-control from a compromised database host.

The security group lacks a description, and combined with the publicly_accessible database it provides no documented intent for the rules attached; rules default behavior should be reviewed to ensure the DB is not reachable beyond the VPC.

findings.issue_category: TLS not enforced for DB connections
findings.description: The MySQL parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = ON, so the application connects to RDS (mysqli_connect without TLS options) over an unencrypted channel, exposing credentials and query data in transit.
